steps.description:
Create a program that asks for 2 words with a space in between. Use split() to separate the words and display them in separate lines.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input chicken egg

one two

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 words separated by space: chicken egg chicken egg

Example 2 Input 2 words separated by space: one two one two
steps.answer:
# ask for 2 words separated by space
text = input("Input 2 words separated by space: ")
# split by space into 2 variables
word1, word2 = text.split()
# display each word on a separate line
print(word1)
print(word2)

steps.description:
Create a program that asks for 3 words with "-" in between and displays the words in separate lines.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input break-it-up

social--distance

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 3 words separated by "-": break-it-up break it up

Example 2 Input 3 words separated by "-": social--distance social

distance

There is a blank line because there is no text between the 2 dashes
steps.answer:
# ask for 3 words separated by dash
text = input('Input 3 words separated by "-": ')
# split by dash into 3 variables
word1, word2, word3 = text.split("-")
# display each word on a separate line
print(word1)
print(word2)
print(word3)

steps.description:
Create a program that asks a student to enter his scores for Art, Geography and History in a row separated by spaces. Display each score in separate lines.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 69.5 82.5 73.4

90 75 85

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input scores for Art, Geography and History: 69.5 82.5 73.4 69.5 82.5 73.4

Example 2 Input scores for Art, Geography and History: 90 75 85 90 75 85
steps.answer:
# ask for 3 scores separated by spaces
text = input("Input scores for Art, Geography and History: ")
# split by space
art, geo, hist = text.split()
# display each score on a separate line
print(art)
print(geo)
print(hist)

steps.description:
Create a program that asks a student to enter his scores for Art, Geography and History in a row separated by spaces. Display the total score.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 69.5 82.5 73.4

90 75 85

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input scores for Art, Geography and History: 69.5 82.5 73.4 225.4

Example 2 Input scores for Art, Geography and History: 90 75 85 250.0
steps.answer:
# ask for 3 scores separated by spaces
text = input("Input scores for Art, Geography and History: ")
# split by space
art, geo, hist = text.split()
# cast to float and add them up
total = float(art) + float(geo) + float(hist)
# display the total
print(total)

steps.description:
Create a program that asks a student to enter his scores for Art, Geography and History in a row separated by spaces. The program will then calculate and display the average score of the subjects rounded to 1 decimal place. The average score is the total score divided by the number of subjects.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 69.5 82.5 73.4

90 75 85

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input scores for Art, Geography and History: 69.5 82.5 73.4 75.1

Example 2 Input scores for Art, Geography and History: 90 75 85 83.3
steps.answer:
# ask for 3 scores separated by spaces
text = input("Input scores for Art, Geography and History: ")
# split by space
art, geo, hist = text.split()
# cast to float and calculate total
total = float(art) + float(geo) + float(hist)
# calculate average (total divided by 3 subjects)
average = total / 3
# round to 1 decimal place and display
print(round(average, 1))
